issues.description: Re-ingest deletes warnings/stats but never clears or reconciles results, so removed or changed input files leave stale rows in the database.
Harness B parsing assumes each JSONL value and metrics field is an object, so valid JSON scalars/lists crash ingest with AttributeError.
Malformed Harness C XML raises ParseError and aborts the entire ingest instead of recording a warning and continuing.
Non-finite scores such as nan bypass range validation and can crash SQLite insertion or persist invalid numeric data.
Harness A accepts blank run_id/model/task values, allowing empty-key collisions and polluted canonical rows.
Harness B accepts missing id/model_name/benchmark values, allowing empty run IDs and meaningless normalized records.
Harness C accepts missing run id/model/task values, allowing empty-key rows and silent overwrites.
Harness A reads but never validates the CSV header, so headerless or reordered files silently lose or mis-map data.
Duplicate run IDs for sources A and C silently overwrite previous rows, while duplicate correction accounting only covers source B.
Report mode creates a new empty SQLite database for a typo or missing path instead of failing loudly.
Fixture generation recursively deletes any existing target directory, creating an avoidable data-loss footgun.
